hints.content: The arrow points to all values less than $5$.
And the point at $5$ is *not* filled in.
So, the inequality represents everything strictly **less than $5$.**

question.content:
**Choose the inequality that represents the following graph.**



[[☃ image 1]]

[[☃ radio 1]]

options.alt: A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the left starts at 5 and continues left. An open point is plotted at 5 where the line begins.

choices.clue:
The graph of $x \leq 5$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the left starts at 5 and continues left. A closed point is plotted at 5 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/6f36c0b9217ed41754f08bb305bfba813d888ab3)

The graph of $x > 5$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the right starts at 5 and continues right. An open point is plotted at 5 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/21bcb879aae133153d1dc997dd2fba29455ba2ad)

The graph of $x \geq 5$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the right starts at 5 and continues right. A closed point is plotted at 5 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/6d18fc5dda69bae834affb385643668f2f430fcf)
